title: Meridian Credit Union: patch management terms
known:
The user is Sam Owner of Larkspur (shown as "You").
Invited: Tom Becker, Larkspur.
Invited: Nina Brooks, Larkspur.
lines: Tom Becker: Thanks for jumping on. So Meridian, the credit union association, picked us over Acumen and Sitewise. But we haven't signed yet.
Tom Becker: And their CMO, Dana Ortiz, sent a note with three things on patching they need before signing.
Tom Becker: One, high vulnerability patches, CVSS seven and up, within forty five days.
Tom Becker: Two, OS and database patches within ninety days regardless of severity.
Tom Becker: And three, every patch decision documented and written into the SOC two.
Nina Brooks: Yeah, they're being extremely clinical. They want a hundred percent proactive coverage. We're opportunistic.
Nina Brooks: The way this reads we'd have to touch eighty to a hundred percent of patches. I can't do that with the staff I have.
Sam Owner (You): What do we do today, Nina?
Nina Brooks: Today we have an SLA for critical and high. Mediums and lows are opportunistic.
Nina Brooks: We decide what applies based on exposure. We apply maybe five percent of available patches. Probably less.
Nina Brooks: There are about eighteen thousand highs in the scanner that just don't apply to us.
Nina Brooks: So the, uh, the forty five ninety I could, I could live without if we were applying the current. We'd keep it at ninety days for, for the rest.
Nina Brooks: and
Tom Becker: Okay so what if we change the text to relevant high vulnerabilities?
Nina Brooks: I could live with the forty five days if we get to decide what applies to us and re-rate the severity. That's what we tell customers today.
Nina Brooks: But I don't want it in the SOC two. If we miss, it's exposed to every other customer in the audit.
Tom Becker: Understood. I don't want to change how we patch. Just the text. Spell it out so it doesn't look like we're just disagreeing.
Sam Owner (You): And on the OS and database one, ninety days regardless of severity, I think we need to tighten that up. Application dependencies aren't a CVSS thing.

Tom Becker: Agreed. Because we would, let's say for instance we'd keep it at ninety days. So the forty five to ninety days is actually not the issue. When I talk to Dana the only thing they want is the forty five days.
Sam Owner (You): Then let's say yes to forty five days for relevant high vulnerabilities, and put the scope in the fine print.
Nina Brooks: Yes. Okay with that.
Tom Becker: Great. Can we amend the document, then I write a cover note and send it back to Dana, and we all sign off together?
Nina Brooks: Fine. Let's do a quick review call at two thirty first.
Tom Becker: Two thirty works. Also, their security lead, Victor, he's going to push back, he wants it watertight.
Nina Brooks: Victor's not pragmatic. I don't want a twice-yearly call with him.
Tom Becker: Fair, we won't offer that.
